value.rationale: Whether a confined diffusing particle eventually reacts when chemical activity is scheduled intermittently is a direct structural question in surface-reaction kinetics. The bounded-profile theorem establishes an exact exposure-only criterion for arbitrary scheduling, together with a sharp covariance constant and universal finite-time survival bound. A smooth unbounded counterexample demonstrates that infinite average/nominal exposure need not produce absorption, and distinguishes almost-sure accumulated contact hazard from its infinite expected value. This is physically and mathematically substantive beyond a routine change of variables.
